chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about a pen made of reeds that is placed in the water for fish, so the fish enter it and some of them die in it. He said, 'There is no harm with it, for that pen is made to be caught with it.'
As for that which indicates that when the dead one is distinguished from the living for him, it is not permissible for him to eat it, is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْحَظِيرَة: A pen or enclosure for catching animals, specifically fish here
key_terms.الْقَصَب: Reeds, the material used to make the pen
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ مِنَ الْحَيِّ: The dead from the living (distinguishing status)
key_terms.لِيُصَادَ بِهَا: To be caught with it (indicating purpose)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish that die inside a fishing net or pen?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam establishes that fish dying in a reed pen (*hazirah*) are permissible because their death is incidental to the primary purpose of capture, distinguishing this from ritual slaughter. The text further clarifies that once the dead are separated from the living, they become distinct entities, implying that their permissibility relies on specific conditions regarding their state and separation, a nuance critical in Shia fiqh regarding aquatic creatures.
